open_issues.impact: A local-only file name containing glob characters could un-track other tracked files at commit time.
open_issues.next: Pass env=_literal_env() to that rm --cached call in a follow-up.
open_issues.text: Same pathspec weakness remains in _step_commit: `git rm --cached -- <untracked local-only paths>` (sync.py ~line 270) takes file names as pathspecs. Left unchanged because the finding named only the conflict-resolution path and the instruction was to change nothing else.

open_issues.impact: The four fixed behaviours have no regression tests.
open_issues.next: Add tests in tests/test_sync.py in a follow-up piece.
open_issues.text: Tests were run only as test_sync and test_remote. No new test was added for the four fixes (late-changed file, glob-named conflict file, deleted remote branch with stale tracking ref, tag named like the branch); tests are outside the stated scope.

summary: sync.py: (1) _recheck_staged re-scans the staged names after git add -A and blocks (PUBLISH_BLOCKED, unstages offenders, rule PS-CHANGED-DURING-SYNC for newly local-only files) if content changed after the first scan; (2) _apply_side runs its git calls with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 so conflict file names are not pathspecs; (3) _step_push asks the remote via ls-remote refs/heads/<branch> instead of trusting the tracking ref, so a deleted remote branch is pushed again; (4) push destination is HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>. tests.test_sync and tests.test_remote pass; no new tests were added.
